definitions: Sensational and often lurid serialized stories published in weekly parts in 19th-century Britain, typically costing one penny.
Cheap, popular fiction of the Victorian era, characterized by thrilling plots and often supernatural or criminal themes.
examples: Victorian readers devoured penny bloods for their thrilling narratives.
The popularity of penny bloods reflected a growing demand for accessible entertainment.
Many penny bloods featured recurring characters and cliffhanger endings.
